**Inputs and outputs:** Spatial coordinates $(\mathbf{x}, y, z)$ and spherical angles $(\theta, \phi)$ are input to produce background and residual density/color predictions [S3].

The claim states that spatial coordinates and spherical angles are inputs to produce background and residual density/color predictions. Since Residual-NeRF-S is a variant of Residual-NeRF and the input mechanism for the NeRF components is described as taking these coordinates and angles, the evidence supports the claim that these are the inputs for producing the respective density and color predictions.

**Edge cases:** Performance drops significantly compared to multi-level models that use positional encodings [S4, unofficial].

The claim states that performance drops significantly compared to multi-level models that use positional encodings. The evidence from Source [S4] explicitly states that 'the model with multi-level sinusoidal encoding functions (NeRF) leads to about 10dB PSNR performance boost' compared to the single-level version (Occupancy Networks) which does not leverage positional encodings. Additionally, it notes that 'single-level DiF models are also consistently worse than the corresponding multi-level models in terms of speed and reconstruction quality.' This confirms that single-level models (without positional encodings) have significantly lower performance than multi-level models (with positional encodings).
